decision: Which approach should we use to migrate the orders table?
context: The orders table holds 400M rows and needs a new indexed column with a backfill. The team has 3 engineers and a 6-hour maintenance window is allowed once a month. Checkout traffic is steady around the clock but dips 70 percent at 3 a.m.

options.name: onewindow
options.text: Run the whole migration inside one monthly window with a rehearsed rollback script.

options.name: shadowtable
options.text: Stream rows into a new table continuously and swap table names once it catches up.

options.name: expandfill
options.text: Add the column as nullable, backfill in small batches for weeks, then enforce it.

options.name: replicaflip
options.text: Migrate a promoted replica offline, validate it, and fail traffic over to it.

decision: Which caching strategy should the product catalogue service adopt?
context: The catalogue API serves 2,000 requests per second at peak, with 85 percent reads and prices changing hourly. Database CPU sits at 75 percent at peak and one engineer can spend three weeks on this. Stale prices have caused refund disputes before.

options.name: cdnedge
options.text: Cache whole responses at the CDN edge with a 60-second time-to-live.

options.name: redisaside
options.text: Add a Redis cache-aside layer with explicit invalidation on price changes.

options.name: localmemory
options.text: Keep a small in-process cache on every instance with a short expiry.

options.name: readreplicas
options.text: Add two read replicas and route the catalogue read queries over to them.

options.name: queryindex
options.text: Rewrite the three slowest queries and add covering indexes instead.

decision: How should the bakery schedule its sourdough fermentation?
context: A small bakery sells 120 loaves daily and has one 8-loaf deck oven plus a walk-in cooler. Two bakers work 4 a.m. starts; a third could join at 2 a.m. for a premium wage. Customers have praised the sour flavour but complained about sell-outs by 10 a.m.

options.name: coldretard
options.text: Shape loaves in the evening and retard them in the cooler overnight.

options.name: warmbulk
options.text: Mix at midnight and ferment warm so loaves bake fresh from 4 a.m. onward.

options.name: splitbatch
options.text: Bake half the loaves from the cold route and half from a warm morning route.

options.name: secondoven
options.text: Rent a second deck oven and keep the current evening-shaping routine unchanged.

decision: Which search backend should the documentation site use?
context: A documentation site has 18,000 pages, 40,000 monthly visitors and a team of two with no search expertise. Hosted search costs 300 a month, self-hosted engines need a server and upkeep, and the current database search is slow and misses typos.

options.name: hostedsaas
options.text: Subscribe to a hosted search service with a ready-made front-end widget.

options.name: selfhosted
options.text: Run an open-source search engine on a small server with nightly indexing.

options.name: dbfulltext
options.text: Tune the existing database full-text search and add a typo-tolerant layer.

options.name: clientindex
options.text: Build a static index at deploy time and search it in the browser.

options.name: embedsearch
options.text: Embed a general web search engine's custom site search for free.

options.name: vectorsearch
options.text: Add a semantic vector search service alongside the keyword search.

decision: Which flour sourcing plan should the pizzeria follow?
context: A pizzeria uses 160 kg of flour weekly, and its dough is sensitive to protein levels. An imported specialty flour costs 1.9 per kg, a regional mill charges 1.1 per kg with batch variation, and storage space holds only two weeks. Pizza prices cannot rise much.

options.name: importedflour
options.text: Order the imported specialty flour monthly in bulk with a long price lock.

options.name: regionalmill
options.text: Buy weekly from the regional mill and adjust hydration for each batch.

options.name: blendmix
options.text: Blend the two flours at a fixed ratio to balance cost and consistency.

options.name: testbatches
options.text: Trial three other mills for a month and then pick the best performer.

options.name: premixed
options.text: Switch to a pre-blended pizza flour from a wholesale distributor.

decision: What should the lab do about its failing minus-80 freezer?
context: The freezer is 14 years old, holds samples from 3 ongoing studies, and has tripped its alarm twice this year. A replacement costs 11,000 and has a 5-week lead time; a repair contract costs 1,800 a year. The department has a shared backup unit that is already 80 percent full.

options.name: replaceunit
options.text: Order a new freezer now and transfer the samples across once it arrives.

options.name: repairplan
options.text: Buy the repair contract and keep running the old unit with daily logging.

options.name: sharebackup
options.text: Move the most irreplaceable samples into the shared backup unit immediately.

options.name: cullsamples
options.text: Audit the inventory and discard low-value samples to fit a smaller unit.

decision: Which candidate profile should we hire for the open support role?
context: A 12-person software shop needs one more support engineer to cut a 36-hour ticket backlog. Budget allows one salary around 52,000, or a contractor at a higher day rate for six months. Onboarding documentation exists but is two years out of date.

options.name: juniorgrow
options.text: Hire a junior generalist and invest roughly a month in structured mentoring.

options.name: seniorfew
options.text: Hire an experienced specialist at the top of the budget who needs little ramp-up.

options.name: contractor
options.text: Engage a six-month contractor to clear the backlog before any permanent hire.

options.name: promoteqa
options.text: Move an existing tester into support and backfill the testing seat later.

decision: Where should the lab spend its 60,000 equipment grant?
context: A university lab of 8 researchers has a 60,000 equipment grant to spend within a year. The shared microscope has 3-week booking queues, the plate reader is 12 years old, and the computing server is nearly out of storage. Two grad students graduate within 18 months.

options.name: newscope
options.text: Buy a second microscope so that the booking queue disappears entirely.

options.name: platereader
options.text: Replace the old plate reader with a current model and a service plan.

options.name: storageserver
options.text: Expand the computing server's storage and add an offsite backup array.

options.name: sharedcore
options.text: Buy time on the institute's core facility and bank the unused funds.

options.name: splitgrant
options.text: Split the grant over smaller repairs and upgrades for all three systems.

decision: What should the catering team serve at the 200-person holiday party?
context: A caterer has a 9,000 budget for 200 guests, a kitchen with two ovens and two staff cooks plus six servers. Dietary needs include 20 vegetarians and 8 gluten-free guests. Last year's plated dinner ran late and cold.

options.name: buffetline
options.text: Serve a hot buffet with two mains and a large vegetable spread.

options.name: platedcourse
options.text: Serve a plated three-course dinner with pre-selected choices.

options.name: foodstations
options.text: Set up four themed food stations that guests visit freely.

options.name: familystyle
options.text: Send shared platters to each table for family-style service.

options.name: passedbites
options.text: Pass hors d'oeuvres all evening with no seated dinner.

options.name: foodtruck
options.text: Hire two food trucks to serve outside for a casual meal.

decision: How should the city handle the eroding riverside footpath?
context: A 1.4 km riverside path used by about 900 walkers and cyclists a day has two collapsing sections. Full stabilisation costs 2.1 million and takes two summers; the capital budget has 600,000 free this year. A parallel street route adds 12 minutes for commuters.

options.name: fullrebuild
options.text: Close the path and rebuild it fully across two summers with bond funding.

options.name: patchfix
options.text: Repair only the two failing sections now and inspect the rest every year.

options.name: reroute
options.text: Move the path 30 metres inland onto city land and abandon the river strip.

options.name: keepopen
options.text: Keep it open with warning signs and a weight limit while seeking grants.

decision: How should I respond to early blight on my tomato plants?
context: About a third of 24 tomato plants show leaf spotting in mid July, with six weeks of harvest left. The beds are raised, drip irrigated, and used for tomatoes three years running. Weather forecasts show a warm, humid fortnight.

options.name: prunespray
options.text: Strip affected lower leaves and spray a copper fungicide weekly until harvest.

options.name: pruneonly
options.text: Strip affected lower leaves, mulch the soil and switch to watering only at the base.

options.name: pullworst
options.text: Remove the eight worst plants entirely to protect the rest of the planting.

options.name: ridethrough
options.text: Take no action beyond monitoring and accept a smaller late-season yield.

decision: Which sales hire should the bakery-supply startup make first?
context: A startup selling bakery equipment has 9 employees, 600,000 revenue and 120,000 earmarked for its first sales hire. Leads come mostly from trade shows, and the founder has closed all deals so far. Sales cycles run 2-3 months.

options.name: seniorrep
options.text: Hire a senior sales rep with industry contacts and a high base salary.

options.name: juniorsdr
options.text: Hire a junior development rep to book meetings for the founder to close.

options.name: commissionrep
options.text: Hire a commission-heavy rep with a low base salary and a firm quota.

options.name: marketer
options.text: Hire a marketer to build inbound leads before adding any sales staff.

options.name: agencydeal
options.text: Contract a sales agency for six months on a retainer plus a success fee.

decision: How should the public API handle a breaking response change?
context: About 340 external integrators call the v2 orders endpoint, and a field rename is needed to fix a long-standing inconsistency. Support has two people and past breaking changes caused 40 tickets. Some integrators are agencies who rarely update their code.

options.name: urlversion
options.text: Ship a new v3 path and keep v2 running for at least eighteen months.

options.name: headerflag
options.text: Let clients opt into the new shape through a request header on the same path.

options.name: dualfields
options.text: Return both old and new field names for a year, then remove the old one.

options.name: hardswitch
options.text: Switch the field on an announced date with a changelog and email notice.

decision: How should the observatory allocate its limited telescope nights?
context: A university observatory has 90 usable nights a year and 14 requests from students and faculty. Past allocation by seniority caused complaints, and weather typically ruins about 40 percent of nights. Two thesis projects have deadlines in the spring.

options.name: seniority
options.text: Allocate nights by seniority as before, with senior staff scheduling.

options.name: peerreview
options.text: Let a rotating committee score proposals and award nights by merit.

options.name: lottery
options.text: Draw lots among all the qualified proposals at the start of each term.

options.name: deadlinefirst
options.text: Give priority to projects with imminent thesis or grant deadlines.

options.name: sharednights
options.text: Split each night between two programmes that have compatible targets.

options.name: remotequeue
options.text: Run a target queue and let staff observe whenever conditions allow.

decision: How should the mid-size city redesign its bus network?
context: A city of 220,000 runs 28 bus routes with an average wait of 24 minutes and falling ridership. The operating budget is flat, and some neighbourhoods would lose service under any redesign. A consultant estimates two years to complete a full overhaul.

options.name: gridfrequent
options.text: Convert to a grid of eight frequent routes and cut the low-use ones.

options.name: keepcoverage
options.text: Keep every route but move service hours toward the commuting peaks.

options.name: microtransit
options.text: Replace the weakest ten routes with an on-demand shuttle service.

options.name: gradual
options.text: Change three routes each year, guided by stop-level ridership counts.

options.name: fareprice
options.text: Make buses free to boost ridership and keep the existing network intact.

decision: How should the youth soccer coach structure practice this season?
context: The under-10 team has 16 players, two 60-minute practices a week and one field shared with another team. Skill levels range widely, and last season three players quit citing boredom. Parents have asked for more games.

options.name: smallsided
options.text: Run most of each practice as rotating small-sided games on half the field.

options.name: stations
options.text: Split the hour into four skill stations with groups matched by ability.

options.name: scrimmage
options.text: Spend the second practice each week as a full scrimmage with mixed teams.

options.name: drillfirst
options.text: Open every practice with 20 minutes of structured drills before any play.

decision: Which piece should the community choir pick for its spring concert?
context: The 38-member choir has two tenors short of a full section, rehearses weekly for 11 weeks, and has a volunteer pianist. Ticket sales fund next year's hall rental, and last spring's all-familiar programme sold out at 180 seats. The conductor wants something more challenging.

options.name: famoussongs
options.text: Sing a medley of well-known folk and pop arrangements with piano accompaniment.

options.name: baroquemass
options.text: Learn a baroque mass in Latin with hired string players for the performance.

options.name: worldmusic
options.text: Perform a set of unaccompanied world songs adapted to the available voices.

options.name: mixedhalf
options.text: Pair a familiar first half with one demanding new piece in the second half.

decision: What should replace the failing front lawn?
context: A 90-square-metre front lawn is patchy, shaded on one side and watered twice a week in summer. The household has a budget of 2,500 and about four weekends of labour. A homeowners' association requires the yard to look tidy but has no strict plant list.

options.name: cloverlawn
options.text: Overseed with a clover and fescue mix and mow the lawn far less often.

options.name: meadowmix
options.text: Plant a native wildflower meadow with a mown edge to keep it tidy.

options.name: gravelbeds
options.text: Lay gravel and drought-tolerant plant beds with a small seating area.

options.name: newsod
options.text: Strip the old lawn and lay new turf with an automatic irrigation timer.

options.name: groundcover
options.text: Plant a low, spreading groundcover that tolerates both sun and shade.

decision: How should the ward schedule nursing shifts for the next quarter?
context: A 24-bed ward employs 18 nurses and uses 12-hour shifts with frequent last-minute swaps. Overtime spend has risen 20 percent, two nurses mention fatigue, and the budget has no room for new hires. Staff are split on shift length.

options.name: twelvefixed
options.text: Keep 12-hour shifts but publish a fixed rotation a quarter ahead.

options.name: eighthour
options.text: Move to eight-hour shifts with a short overlap for the handover.

options.name: selfschedule
options.text: Let nurses bid for shifts in a self-scheduling system with fair rules.

options.name: floatpool
options.text: Create a small float pool of nurses who fill gaps across the wards.

options.name: agencycover
options.text: Use agency nurses for the peak weeks to cut regular staff overtime.

options.name: mixedlength
options.text: Offer a mix of eight- and twelve-hour shifts, chosen by each nurse.

decision: What should we do about the aging flat roof section?
context: A 22-square-metre flat roof over the kitchen is 17 years old and has leaked twice in heavy rain. A full membrane replacement is quoted at 6,500; patch repair is quoted at 700 with a two-year guarantee. A kitchen renovation is planned for roughly 18 months out.

options.name: fullmembrane
options.text: Replace the whole membrane now and take the 20-year manufacturer warranty.

options.name: patchrepair
options.text: Patch the leaking seams now and re-evaluate when the renovation begins.

options.name: coatingsystem
options.text: Apply a liquid coating over the existing surface for roughly ten more years.

options.name: bundlereno
options.text: Patch now and fold a full new roof into the kitchen renovation contract.

decision: Which venue should host the 250-person alumni reunion?
context: The reunion is in 14 weeks with a budget of 18,000, and about a third of attendees travel from out of town. Options differ in capacity, location and what they include. A mid-week date is possible but weekends have higher attendance in past years.

options.name: hotelballroom
options.text: Book the hotel ballroom with in-house catering and a discounted room block.

options.name: campushall
options.text: Use the campus hall at low rent and hire outside caterers and equipment.

options.name: breweryspace
options.text: Reserve a brewery event space with a flat food-and-drink package.

options.name: splitevents
options.text: Hold a smaller dinner for 120 plus an open afternoon picnic for everyone.

decision: Which surface should the club choose for its new pitch?
context: A local football club with 300 members has 450,000 raised for one new pitch. Natural grass costs less up front but needs rest between matches; artificial turf costs more but allows evening and winter use. Members disagree about injury concerns.

options.name: naturalgrass
options.text: Lay a natural grass pitch and rest it every third week to let it recover.

options.name: artificialturf
options.text: Lay a full artificial turf pitch with floodlights for evening sessions.

options.name: hybridturf
options.text: Install a hybrid pitch where natural grass is reinforced by synthetic fibres.

options.name: sandbased
options.text: Build a sand-based grass pitch with deep drainage to allow winter play.

options.name: smallturf
options.text: Build a smaller artificial pitch for training and keep grass for matches.

decision: How should the food bank spend its 15,000 surplus grant?
context: The food bank serves about 600 households a month from a rented warehouse and has a 15,000 one-time grant with a 90-day spending deadline. Fresh produce demand is rising, the single refrigerator breaks down often, and two volunteer drivers recently left.

options.name: coldstorage
options.text: Buy a commercial walk-in cooler to handle fresh produce reliably.

options.name: usedvan
options.text: Purchase a used delivery van and pay a part-time driver stipend.

options.name: bulkbuying
options.text: Spend it on bulk non-perishable purchases to stock shelves for the winter.

options.name: reservefund
options.text: Hold part as a reserve and spend only on the cooler repair this quarter.

decision: How should the teacher arrange the classroom this term?
context: A teacher of 30 eleven-year-olds has a rectangular room, noisy corridor and several students with attention difficulties. Group work is required by the curriculum for about a third of lessons. Furniture can be moved in 5 minutes but the room has one power outlet.

options.name: rows
options.text: Seat students in rows facing the board for most lessons and tasks.

options.name: pods
options.text: Seat students in pods of five to support group work and discussion.

options.name: ushape
options.text: Arrange desks in a U-shape so that everyone faces teacher and peers.

options.name: flexible
options.text: Provide flexible seating options and let students choose by the task.

options.name: rotating
options.text: Rotate the layout each week between rows and pods by lesson type.

options.name: pairs
options.text: Seat students in pairs facing forward and use pair talk for tasks.

decision: How should the touring quartet plan its autumn dates?
context: A string quartet has a six-week window in October and November, a shared van and a 15,000 travel budget. Past regional gigs paid 800 each, while a city residency offered 6,000 for the month. Two members teach during the week.

options.name: regionaltour
options.text: Play twelve regional venues on weekends and drive between them in the van.

options.name: citystay
options.text: Take the month-long city residency and fit the teaching around the shows.

options.name: festivals
options.text: Apply to three festivals and accept whichever of them confirms first.

options.name: houseconcerts
options.text: Book private house concerts at higher fees but with smaller audiences.

options.name: recordalbum
options.text: Skip touring entirely and use the six-week window to record a studio album.

decision: How should the clinic redesign its appointment check-in process?
context: A 6-doctor outpatient clinic sees roughly 140 visits a day, and front-desk check-in averages 7 minutes per person. Forms are on paper; 30 percent of patients are over 70. A tablet kiosk costs 4,000 each and staff worry about a long learning curve.

options.name: kiosks
options.text: Install two self-service kiosks and keep one staffed desk for assistance.

options.name: prefilled
options.text: Send digital forms the day before and keep the desk for verification only.

options.name: extrastaff
options.text: Add a second front-desk employee during the peak morning hours each day.

options.name: shortforms
options.text: Cut the paper forms to one page and keep the process otherwise unchanged.

decision: Which seed supplier arrangement should the 80-hectare farm choose?
context: The farm grows maize and soybeans on 80 hectares with thin margins and two bad harvests in the last six years. A national supplier offers a 6 percent discount on a 3-year contract; a local co-op sells at list price but allows returns. Seed demand peaks suddenly in spring.

options.name: natcontract
options.text: Sign the three-year national contract to lock in the six percent discount.

options.name: localcoop
options.text: Buy yearly from the local co-op and keep the flexibility to return seed.

options.name: mixedsupply
options.text: Split purchases, taking half under contract and half from the co-op.

options.name: savedseed
options.text: Save and clean part of last year's soybean seed to cut input costs.

decision: How should we address the old wiring in this 1960s house?
context: A 1960s house has partly cloth-covered wiring, an old fuse board and one kitchen circuit that trips regularly. A full rewire is quoted at 9,500 and takes 8 days with the household out. An inspector found no immediate fire hazard.

options.name: fullrewire
options.text: Rewire the whole house and replace the fuse board in one single project.

options.name: staged
options.text: Rewire the kitchen and upstairs this year and the rest in two years' time.

options.name: boardonly
options.text: Replace the fuse board and add residual-current protection, keep the wiring.

options.name: repairkitchen
options.text: Repair just the problem kitchen circuit and retest the rest annually.

options.name: sellasis
options.text: Leave it and disclose the condition to buyers when selling in three years.

decision: How should the pottery studio expand its firing capacity?
context: A pottery studio with 25 students and a 90-litre electric kiln fires twice weekly and has a two-week queue. A larger 200-litre kiln costs 6,500 and needs a new electrical circuit, a second small kiln costs 2,300 and uses the existing power. Rent is 900 a month.

options.name: largekiln
options.text: Buy the 200-litre kiln and pay for the new dedicated electrical circuit.

options.name: smallkiln
options.text: Buy a second small kiln and run both on staggered firing schedules.

options.name: gaskiln
options.text: Buy a used gas kiln, which fires faster but needs a vented space nearby.

options.name: outsourcefire
options.text: Pay a nearby studio by the shelf to fire the overflow of student work.

options.name: limitclasses
options.text: Cap student pieces per term and keep the current single kiln as it is.

options.name: wholesalefire
options.text: Sell a firing service to outside potters to fund a larger kiln later.

decision: How many copies should the small press print for its debut novel?
context: A small press has a debut novel releasing in October and a 9,000 print budget. Offset printing 1,500 copies costs 4.20 each, while print-on-demand costs 7.80 per copy with no stock. The author has a modest local following and one confirmed bookstore chain order of 300.

options.name: offset1500
options.text: Print 1,500 copies by offset and hold the remaining stock in a rented unit.

options.name: offset600
options.text: Print 600 copies by offset and reprint if the first run sells through.

options.name: ondemand
options.text: Use print-on-demand for all orders and spend the savings on advertising.

options.name: hybridrun
options.text: Print 400 offset copies for the chain order and use on-demand for the rest.

decision: Should the shop run a flash sale before the holiday season?
context: A homewares shop has 14,000 of slow stock, a 32 percent gross margin and a busy period starting in six weeks. Previous discounts of 20 percent brought a spike that fell back within days. The owner worries about teaching customers to wait for sales.

options.name: deepdiscount
options.text: Run a 35 percent clearance event for one weekend to free cash and space.

options.name: bundles
options.text: Pair slow items with bestsellers in bundles at a small combined discount.

options.name: liquidator
options.text: Sell the whole slow stock in one lot to a liquidator at a steep loss.

options.name: holdstock
options.text: Hold the stock at regular prices and give it prime shelf position up front.

decision: How should the couple structure a 120-guest wedding on 20,000?
context: A couple has 20,000 and expects 120 guests, a quarter travelling by air. Venues quote 8,000 to 14,000 on weekends and about 35 percent less on Fridays. Both sets of parents offered small contributions but with opinions.

options.name: fridaydate
options.text: Choose a Friday date and put the venue savings toward much better food.

options.name: smallguest
options.text: Cut the guest list to 70 people and keep the more popular weekend date.

options.name: backyard
options.text: Host at a family garden with rented tents and a hired outside caterer.

options.name: destination
options.text: Marry at a destination with 30 guests and hold a party at home later.

options.name: parentsmoney
options.text: Accept the parents' contributions and expand the total budget to 26,000.

decision: How should on-call handle a flood of noisy alerts?
context: The on-call rota of 7 engineers receives about 90 pages a week, and roughly 60 percent need no action. Two engineers have asked to leave the rota, and two real outages were slow to notice last quarter. A quarter of the alerts come from one legacy service.

options.name: tunethresholds
options.text: Spend two sprints tuning thresholds and deleting alerts that never needed action.

options.name: tierpages
options.text: Split alerts into page and ticket tiers so only urgent ones wake people.

options.name: paidtool
options.text: Buy an alert-grouping product and let it deduplicate pages automatically.

options.name: retirelegacy
options.text: Prioritise retiring the legacy service that generates a quarter of the noise.

decision: What should the city do with the downtown surface parking lot?
context: A 0.8-hectare city-owned parking lot downtown has 140 spaces and earns 160,000 a year. Nearby shops rely on it, a housing group wants affordable units, and the council has a 3 million capital gap. A rezoning process takes 18 months.

options.name: sellhousing
options.text: Sell the land to a developer under an affordable housing requirement.

options.name: longlease
options.text: Lease it for 50 years to a developer while the city keeps ownership.

options.name: parkinggarage
options.text: Build a multi-storey garage to keep the parking and add more capacity.

options.name: publicplaza
options.text: Convert it to a public plaza with a weekly market and some seating.

options.name: pricedparking
options.text: Keep it as a surface lot but raise prices and shorten the stay limits.

options.name: mixeduse
options.text: Develop it in two phases, housing on one half and parking on the other.

decision: How should the small museum respond to a 20 percent grant cut?
context: A local history museum with 6 staff and 40 volunteers loses a 24,000 annual grant. Admission is 5 and visits are about 9,000 a year, mostly school groups. The board is wary of changing the free school programme.

options.name: raisedmission
options.text: Raise admission from 5 to 8 and keep every current programme running.

options.name: cuthours
options.text: Close two days a week and cut staff hours to match the lower income.

options.name: rentspace
options.text: Rent the main hall for events and accept some disruption to exhibits.

options.name: membership
options.text: Launch a paid membership drive with early-access exhibit previews.

options.name: newgrants
options.text: Trim spending lightly and spend a year applying for replacement grants.

decision: What should replace the company's quarterly password rotation rule?
context: Employees at a 300-person firm reset passwords every 90 days, and helpdesk spends about 15 hours a week on lockouts. A recent phishing test caught 22 percent of staff. Hardware keys cost 45 each and some staff work on shared kiosks.

options.name: hardwarekeys
options.text: Issue hardware security keys to all staff and drop forced rotation.

options.name: passkeysmfa
options.text: Move to app-based multi-factor sign-in and keep passwords without rotation.

options.name: manager
options.text: Roll out a company password manager with long generated passwords.

options.name: keeprotation
options.text: Keep rotation but lengthen the interval to 180 days and add breach checks.

decision: How should the data team approach predicting subscriber churn?
context: A subscription app has 90,000 paying users, a 4 percent monthly churn and one data analyst plus a part-time engineer. Marketing wants a list of at-risk users within 6 weeks. Usage logs are clean for the last 10 months only.

options.name: gradientboost
options.text: Train a gradient-boosted model on usage features and score users weekly.

options.name: simplerules
options.text: Write transparent rules from a few engagement signals and review monthly.

options.name: survival
options.text: Fit a survival model that estimates how long each user is likely to stay.

options.name: vendorscore
options.text: Buy a hosted churn-scoring service and feed it the existing usage logs.

decision: How should the clinic office handle its insurance-claim backlog?
context: A dental clinic has 640 unpaid insurance claims, about 120,000 of billed value, and one billing clerk working 30 hours a week. Roughly 18 percent of claims are rejected for coding errors. A billing service takes 6 percent of collections.

options.name: outsource
options.text: Hand the entire backlog to an outside billing service for a percentage fee.

options.name: overtime
options.text: Pay the clerk overtime for eight weeks so that the backlog gets cleared.

options.name: temphelp
options.text: Hire a temporary claims specialist for three months to work the backlog.

options.name: oldestfirst
options.text: Process claims strictly oldest first and ignore small-value claims.

options.name: fixcoding
options.text: Spend two weeks fixing the coding errors before working the backlog.

decision: Which fruit trees should we plant in the backyard orchard?
context: A homeowner has room for six trees on a south-facing slope with clay soil and cold winters to minus 18 degrees. The household wants fruit within five years and low spray effort. A neighbour already grows two apple trees.

options.name: applesdwarf
options.text: Plant six dwarf apple trees of varieties chosen for disease resistance.

options.name: pearsplum
options.text: Plant three pear trees and three plum trees for staggered harvests.

options.name: cherries
options.text: Plant two sour cherry trees and four hardy apples for early fruit.

options.name: nutsmix
options.text: Plant hazelnut bushes and one walnut tree for low-maintenance crops.

options.name: bushfruit
options.text: Plant currants and gooseberries as shrubs in place of any fruit trees.

options.name: mixedsix
options.text: Plant one tree each of apple, pear, plum, cherry, apricot and quince.

decision: How should the community garden manage water over summer?
context: A community garden with 40 plots has a single tap, a 1,000-litre rain tank and water bills of 85 a month in summer. Members split on rules, and several plots are tended by people who visit only on weekends. Past droughts led to rationing arguments.

options.name: dripsystem
options.text: Install timer-controlled drip lines on every plot from a central manifold.

options.name: moretanks
options.text: Add three more rain tanks and keep hand watering with fair-use rules.

options.name: mulchrule
options.text: Require mulch on all plots and restrict watering to two scheduled evenings.

options.name: sharedwatering
options.text: Assign a rotating volunteer crew to water all plots on a fixed route.

decision: How should we pace a two-week trip through Japan with a child?
context: Two adults and a 7-year-old plan 14 days in late October, with a 6,000 budget excluding flights. The child tires by mid-afternoon, and rail passes are cheaper only if five long trips are made. The parents want both cities and countryside.

options.name: twobases
options.text: Use two bases, Tokyo and Kyoto, and make easy day trips from each one.

options.name: fourstops
options.text: Move through four stops with a rail pass and short stays of three nights.

options.name: slowrural
options.text: Spend most of the time in one quiet countryside region with few transfers.

options.name: splitpace
options.text: Alternate busy city days with rest days in a single apartment rental.

decision: Which irrigation upgrade should the orchard install?
context: A 15-hectare apple orchard uses flood irrigation, faces water restrictions in dry months, and has a 40,000 loan limit. Drip lines cost about 3,600 per hectare, micro-sprinklers 2,200 per hectare, and soil sensors 5,000 for the farm. Yields have dipped in the last two droughts.

options.name: dripall
options.text: Install drip lines on all 15 hectares of the orchard over two seasons.

options.name: dripblocks
options.text: Install drip on the six most drought-sensitive hectares in the first year.

options.name: microsprinkle
options.text: Install micro-sprinklers across the orchard, doubling as frost protection.

options.name: sensorsonly
options.text: Buy soil sensors and schedule the existing flood irrigation by readings.

options.name: mulchcover
options.text: Apply deep mulch and sow cover crops and keep the current irrigation.

decision: How should the teacher assess the semester's chemistry unit?
context: A teacher has 28 students, 8 weeks left and a state exam at term end. Previous cohorts scored well on labs but poorly on multi-step calculation questions. Marking a project for everyone takes about 20 hours.

options.name: weeklyquiz
options.text: Give a short quiz every week and drop the lowest two scores.

options.name: labproject
options.text: Assign a graded lab project with a written analysis due at week seven.

options.name: midtest
options.text: Hold one long midterm test and a retake opportunity before the exam.

options.name: peerreview
options.text: Use peer-marked problem sets with spot checks by the teacher.

decision: How should the swim club restructure its membership fees?
context: A swim club of 210 members charges a flat 40 a month, runs a 25-metre pool leased for 4,800 a month, and has a waiting list for lane time at peak hours. Families complain about cost, and competitive swimmers want more lanes.

options.name: peakpricing
options.text: Charge more for the peak lane hours and less for off-peak lane times.

options.name: tiered
options.text: Offer basic and competitive membership tiers at two different prices.

options.name: familycap
options.text: Cap the total monthly charge per family at a clearly lower amount.

options.name: flatraise
options.text: Raise the flat fee by 5 and keep the structure otherwise unchanged.

options.name: sponsorship
options.text: Seek local business sponsors and keep fees at their current level.

options.name: extrapool
options.text: Lease extra pool hours and add a junior-only session at off-peak times.

decision: Which cover direction should the poetry collection use?
context: A small press prints 800 copies of a poetry collection with a 400 design budget and a three-week deadline. Bookshop buyers say poetry covers blend together, and the poet likes an abstract painting she made. Online sales rely on tiny thumbnail images.

options.name: poetpainting
options.text: Use the poet's own abstract painting full-bleed with only minimal text.

options.name: boldtype
options.text: Use a bold typographic cover with a large title and a single colour.

options.name: illustrator
options.text: Commission an illustrator for a distinctive image within the budget.

options.name: photocover
options.text: License a stock photograph and set the title large across the top of it.

options.name: plainfoil
options.text: Use a restrained plain cover with a foil-stamped title and no image.

decision: How should the courier restructure its delivery routes?
context: A regional courier runs 22 vans delivering to about 1,900 addresses daily, with 11 percent failed first attempts. Drivers know their areas well, and a route-optimisation tool costs 600 per van per year. Several customers ask for fixed afternoon time windows.

options.name: optimiser
options.text: Subscribe to the optimisation tool and re-plan routes every morning.

options.name: fixedzones
options.text: Assign each driver a fixed zone and keep routes stable for familiarity.

options.name: timewindows
options.text: Offer two-hour delivery windows and sequence stops around them.

options.name: lockerhubs
options.text: Set up neighbourhood locker points for customers who miss deliveries.

decision: How should the beekeeper grow from 12 to 20 hives?
context: A hobbyist sells honey at a weekly market and has two years of experience with 12 colonies. New nucleus colonies cost 160 each; splitting existing hives is free but weakens them. Winter losses last year were 25 percent.

options.name: buynucs
options.text: Buy eight nucleus colonies in spring from a local breeder.

options.name: splithives
options.text: Split the strongest colonies in early summer and raise new queens.

options.name: catchswarms
options.text: Set swarm traps and register with the local swarm-collection list.

options.name: hold12
options.text: Stay at 12 hives for another year and focus on winter survival.

decision: How should the independent bookstore rearrange its floor?
context: A 140-square-metre bookstore earns 22 percent of revenue from the cafe corner, and bestsellers sit at the front. Customers often ask for staff recommendations, and the children's section is cramped. A full rearrangement costs 6,000 and a week of closure.

options.name: cafeexpand
options.text: Expand the cafe corner and shrink the fiction shelving to make room for it.

options.name: kidsroom
options.text: Enlarge the children's section into the back room and add reading seating.

options.name: curated
options.text: Reorganise shelves by theme with staff-recommendation tables at the front.

options.name: lightchange
options.text: Move only the front tables and signage, working over a single weekend.

options.name: eventspace
options.text: Make the centre floor flexible with movable shelves for evening events.

decision: Which act should the festival book as Saturday's headliner?
context: A small outdoor festival expects 2,500 people and has a 30,000 headliner budget. A veteran act asks 28,000 but is reliable, a rising act asks 12,000 and may sell out later, and a local favourite asks 6,000. Rain is possible, and the stage is covered.

options.name: veteranact
options.text: Book the veteran act at nearly the full headliner budget available.

options.name: risingact
options.text: Book the rising act and spend the savings on production and a stage.

options.name: localhero
options.text: Book the local favourite and several smaller supporting acts as well.

options.name: twomid
options.text: Book two mid-level acts at 14,000 each and share the headline slot.

options.name: tributeband
options.text: Book a well-known tribute band at a modest fee for familiar songs.

options.name: djclose
options.text: Book a closing DJ set to follow a somewhat shorter live music programme.

decision: Should we spend the 40,000 savings on the house down payment?
context: A couple has 40,000 saved, steady salaries, and rent of 1,450 a month. A modest starter home needs about 55,000 down for a comfortable loan, or 40,000 with higher monthly costs and insurance. They may relocate within five years for work.

options.name: buynow
options.text: Buy the starter home now with the smaller down payment and higher costs.

options.name: saveyear
options.text: Keep renting for another year while saving to reach the larger down payment.

options.name: cheapercity
options.text: Buy a cheaper property in a nearby town where the 40,000 goes further.

options.name: investrent
options.text: Keep renting indefinitely and place the savings in a broad index fund.

decision: How should the team roll out the new checkout page?
context: The checkout redesign passed internal testing and handles about 12,000 orders a day. Last year a redesign cut conversion by 3 percent for two weeks before a fix. The team of 5 has no experimentation platform, only a feature-flag tool.

options.name: percentramp
options.text: Ramp from 5 to 100 percent of traffic over two weeks with metric checks.

options.name: abtest
options.text: Run a formal 50-50 split test for four weeks before deciding to ship.

options.name: regionfirst
options.text: Release to one small country first and then expand market by market.

options.name: bigbang
options.text: Launch to everyone at once on a quiet Tuesday with a one-click rollback.

decision: Which backup strategy should the small company adopt?
context: A 25-person company keeps 3 TB of files on a single office server and a cloud drive. A drive failure last year cost two days of work. Budget is 1,200 a year, and nobody on staff is dedicated to IT.

options.name: cloudbackup
options.text: Subscribe to an automatic cloud backup service for the server.

options.name: nasmirror
options.text: Buy a second network storage unit and mirror nightly to it.

options.name: offsitedisks
options.text: Rotate encrypted external disks to an employee's home each week.

options.name: moveall
options.text: Move everything into the cloud drive and retire the office server.

options.name: tapebackup
options.text: Use a tape drive with weekly full and daily incremental backups.

decision: How should the summer camp staff its 8-week programme?
context: A nonprofit camp serves 90 children a week and has 6 returning counselors and funds for 6 more hires. Applicants are mostly 18-year-old students who leave in August; older applicants want fewer weeks. Last year three counselors left mid-season.

options.name: students
options.text: Hire eight student counselors for the full season and train them in June.

options.name: olderstaff
options.text: Hire older counselors on flexible shifts even though they cover fewer weeks.

options.name: shortcontracts
options.text: Staff in two four-week blocks with separate groups of counselors.

options.name: volunteers
options.text: Add a volunteer parent rota to reduce the number of paid hires needed.

decision: How should we replace the drafty windows in our house?
context: A 1980s house has 11 single-glazed wooden windows, and winter heating costs 1,900. Full triple-glazed replacements are quoted at 12,000, secondary glazing at 3,800, and draft sealing with storm panels at 900. The house is planned to be sold in 6 years.

options.name: triplenew
options.text: Replace all windows with triple-glazed units in one single project.

options.name: secondary
options.text: Install secondary glazing panels inside each of the existing windows.

options.name: stormpanels
options.text: Seal the drafts and fit removable storm panels every winter season.

options.name: northfirst
options.text: Replace only the five north-facing windows now and leave the rest.

options.name: refurbish
options.text: Have a joiner refurbish and weatherstrip the existing wooden windows.

options.name: heavycurtain
options.text: Install thermal curtains and cellular blinds and leave the windows alone.

decision: How should the app redesign its first-run onboarding?
context: A budgeting app loses 55 percent of new users before completing setup, which takes 9 screens. User research shows people want quick value, but regulators require identity checks for linked accounts. The design team has one designer and four weeks.

options.name: shortsetup
options.text: Cut setup to three screens and defer account linking until later.

options.name: guidedtour
options.text: Add an interactive guided tour while keeping the nine screens.

options.name: demomode
options.text: Offer a pre-filled demo mode and ask for signup afterwards.

options.name: progressbar
options.text: Keep the screens but add a progress bar and save-and-resume.

options.name: emailseq
options.text: Keep onboarding as is and add a five-email nudge sequence.

decision: How long should our sprints be going forward?
context: A team of 9 runs two-week sprints and spends roughly 15 percent of each sprint in ceremonies. Stakeholders ask for faster feedback, but the last attempt at one-week sprints caused rushed reviews. About a third of work items span more than one sprint.

options.name: oneweek
options.text: Move to one-week sprints with shorter ceremonies and smaller items.

options.name: threeweek
options.text: Stretch to three-week sprints with fewer ceremonies and fewer carry-overs.

options.name: keeptwo
options.text: Keep two-week sprints but trim ceremonies and hold demos more often.

options.name: flowboard
options.text: Drop sprints for a continuous flow board with weekly priority reviews.

decision: Which compost system suits a family of four with a small yard?
context: A family produces about 8 litres of kitchen scraps a week and has a 25-square-metre yard with a shaded corner. Neighbours are close, and a previous heap attracted rats. They want finished compost for raised beds by next spring.

options.name: tumbler
options.text: Buy a closed two-chamber tumbler and turn it daily to speed decomposition.

options.name: woodbins
options.text: Build three wooden bins in the yard and turn the heap every two weeks.

options.name: wormbin
options.text: Keep a worm bin on the porch and harvest castings every few months.

options.name: citycollect
options.text: Use the city's organic waste collection and buy finished compost instead.

decision: What lab notebook system should the group move to?
context: A microbiology group of 12 uses paper notebooks and has lost data twice when notebooks were damaged. An electronic system costs 90 per user per year, and several senior members dislike typing at the bench. A funder will soon require data-management plans.

options.name: fullelectronic
options.text: Adopt an electronic notebook for everyone with a three-month transition.

options.name: scanpaper
options.text: Keep paper notebooks and scan every page each week to a shared drive.

options.name: hybrid
options.text: Let each researcher choose, with a mandatory weekly digital summary.

options.name: tabletbench
options.text: Provide stylus tablets at the benches for handwritten electronic notes.

options.name: pilotteam
options.text: Pilot the electronic system with three people for one semester first.

decision: How should the small brand run its booth at the trade fair?
context: A craft-goods brand has a 4,000 fair budget for a 3 by 3 metre booth and two staff for three days. Last year it collected 90 leads and 12 orders. A bigger booth costs an extra 1,500, and a nearby workshop slot costs 600.

options.name: biggerbooth
options.text: Upgrade to the larger booth and run a live product demonstration.

options.name: samebooth
options.text: Keep the same booth size and invest in a better lead-capture process.

options.name: workshopslot
options.text: Book the nearby workshop slot to host a hands-on session for buyers.

options.name: sampleboxes
options.text: Give out sample boxes to buyers who leave a business card with us.

options.name: sharebooth
options.text: Share a booth with a complementary brand and split all the costs.

options.name: skipfair
options.text: Skip the fair and spend the budget on direct outreach to retailers.

decision: How should the school distribute its 50,000 financial aid pool?
context: A private school of 420 students has a 50,000 aid pool and 60 families asking for help. Aid decisions are made by a committee and some families have just missed the income cutoff. Enrolment is slightly below target for next year.

options.name: fewfull
options.text: Give full awards to the ten neediest families and decline the others.

options.name: manypartial
options.text: Give partial awards to every family that meets the published income cutoff.

options.name: tiered
options.text: Create three aid tiers by income band, each with a fixed award amount.

options.name: bursary
options.text: Set half aside as an emergency fund for hardship cases arising mid-year.

decision: How should the 400-person conference fill its two-day schedule?
context: A regional developer conference has three rooms and 55 accepted proposals of mixed quality. Last year's attendees complained about too many overlapping tracks and short breaks. Sponsors want time on stage.

options.name: singletrack
options.text: Run a single main track with every talk and fewer, longer breaks.

options.name: threetracks
options.text: Run three parallel tracks so that every accepted talk gets a slot.

options.name: curatedtwo
options.text: Cut to 30 talks across two tracks and add open workshops between them.

options.name: unconference
options.text: Make the second day an unconference that attendees plan on the spot.

decision: Which kitchen staffing mix should the restaurant choose?
context: A 60-seat restaurant has a head chef, one sous chef and turnover of about 50 percent a year among line cooks. A culinary school graduate costs 14 per hour, an experienced cook 21 per hour, and agency staff 28 per hour. Friday and Saturday are the busiest days.

options.name: graduates
options.text: Hire two graduates and train them on the restaurant's own menu and methods.

options.name: experienced
options.text: Hire one experienced cook and add a part-time dishwasher to the team.

options.name: agency
options.text: Use agency cooks on weekends and keep the existing team on weekdays.

options.name: cross
options.text: Cross-train the servers to do prep work during the quiet afternoons.

options.name: trimmenu
options.text: Shrink the menu to fit the current team and avoid making any new hires.

decision: Which sump pump setup should we install in the basement?
context: A basement flooded twice in four years during storms, and power outages occurred both times. A standard pump costs 450 installed, a battery backup system costs 1,300, and a water-powered backup runs on city pressure and costs 900. Neighbours report occasional low water pressure.

options.name: standardpump
options.text: Install one standard electric pump and test it at the start of each season.

options.name: batterybackup
options.text: Install a primary pump with a battery backup unit and a failure alarm.

options.name: waterbackup
options.text: Install a primary pump with a water-powered backup on city pressure.

options.name: exteriordrain
options.text: Add exterior drainage and regrade the yard before any pump upgrades.

decision: How should the animal shelter limit overcrowding this summer?
context: An animal shelter built for 60 dogs holds 84, adoption rates dip in summer, and foster volunteers number 22. Euthanasia is not used for space, and the budget has 7,000 spare. Vet costs are rising and kennel stress is causing behaviour problems.

options.name: fosterdrive
options.text: Run a foster recruitment drive with a supplies stipend for volunteers.

options.name: adoptionpromo
options.text: Run reduced-fee adoption events at the shelter every weekend in summer.

options.name: limitintake
options.text: Pause non-emergency intake and refer owners to other support services.

options.name: transfers
options.text: Transfer 15 dogs to shelters in less crowded regions of the country.

options.name: tempkennels
options.text: Rent temporary kennel space off-site for the duration of the summer.

options.name: spayclinic
options.text: Fund a low-cost neutering clinic to reduce the shelter's future intake.

decision: How should the city handle congestion on its only river bridge?
context: A town of 60,000 has one bridge carrying 38,000 vehicles a day, with 40-minute delays at peaks. A second bridge would cost 80 million and take 7 years. Bus lanes, tolls and staggered work hours are cheaper but each affect different groups.

options.name: secondbridge
options.text: Build a second bridge over seven years and phase in tolls to fund it.

options.name: buslane
options.text: Dedicate one lane to buses and shuttle service during the peak hours.

options.name: congestionfee
options.text: Charge a peak-hour fee on the bridge and invest the income in transit.

options.name: stagger
options.text: Work with the largest employers to stagger their shift start times.

options.name: ferry
options.text: Start a commuter ferry service from the two busiest neighbourhoods.

decision: How should I start vegetables for a 30-bed market garden?
context: A new market garden has 30 beds, a heated greenhouse bench for 800 seedling cells and a six-week window before the last frost. Buying transplants costs about 0.45 each, while sowing in-house takes daily attention. The grower has a part-time job.

options.name: allgreenhouse
options.text: Sow everything in the greenhouse and monitor the seedlings twice daily.

options.name: buyplants
options.text: Buy all transplants from a nursery and skip the heated bench entirely.

options.name: directsow
options.text: Direct sow tolerant crops and start only tomatoes and peppers indoors.

options.name: coldframes
options.text: Use unheated cold frames for everything and accept a later start date.

options.name: swapnursery
options.text: Share the bench with a neighbour grower who handles weekday watering.

decision: How should we fix the slow and flaky test suite?
context: A web application's test suite runs 38 minutes and fails randomly about 8 percent of runs. Seven developers merge about 25 pull requests a day. Fixing flakes could take months, but parallel runners cost 400 a month.

options.name: parallelrun
options.text: Pay for parallel runners to cut the total run to roughly ten minutes.

options.name: quarantine
options.text: Move flaky tests into a separate non-blocking job and fix them slowly.

options.name: selecttests
options.text: Run only the tests affected by each change on pull requests.

options.name: prunetests
options.text: Delete the slowest low-value end-to-end tests from the whole suite.

options.name: rewriteslow
options.text: Rewrite the slowest tests as faster integration tests over one sprint.

options.name: nightlyfull
options.text: Run the full suite nightly and a small smoke suite on each change.

decision: How should the music school structure trial lessons?
context: A music school with 14 teachers loses about a third of trial students before they enrol. Trial lessons are free and last 30 minutes, taking up teacher time that could earn 30 per hour. Parents say they want to compare teachers.

options.name: paidtrial
options.text: Charge a small fee for each trial lesson and credit it on enrolment.

options.name: grouptrial
options.text: Replace single trials with a free weekend group workshop for newcomers.

options.name: trialpackage
options.text: Sell a three-lesson starter package at a discount instead of one trial.

options.name: freeunchanged
options.text: Keep free trials but add a personal follow-up call within two days.

options.name: videointro
options.text: Publish teacher videos and offer trials only to those who request one.

decision: How long should we retain customer support chat logs?
context: A software company stores 5 years of support chats, 2 TB in total, with some containing personal data. Legal suggests a maximum of three years, support teams use old chats for training, and a breach would expose all of them.

options.name: oneyear
options.text: Keep logs for one year and then delete them automatically for good.

options.name: threeyears
options.text: Keep logs for three years with access limited to the support leads.

options.name: anonymise
options.text: Keep logs for five years but strip all personal data after one year.

options.name: sampleonly
options.text: Delete most logs at one year and keep a curated sample for training.

options.name: userchoice
options.text: Delete a customer's logs on request and keep the rest for three years.

options.name: coldarchive
options.text: Move old logs to encrypted cold storage and require approval to access.

decision: What footwear plan should the beginning ultrarunner follow?
context: A runner preparing for a 50 km trail race in 14 weeks has 400 monthly kilometres, an old pair with 700 km and flat feet. Trail shoes cost around 140, and last year she had shin pain. Race terrain is rocky with wet sections.

options.name: onepair
options.text: Buy one cushioned trail shoe now and use it for all the long runs.

options.name: rotation
options.text: Buy two different models and rotate them across the training week.

options.name: keepold
options.text: Keep running in the old pair and buy race shoes in the final month.

options.name: fitting
options.text: Pay for a professional gait fitting before choosing any shoes at all.

options.name: roadhybrid
options.text: Choose a road-to-trail hybrid shoe that also works for daily runs.

decision: How should the band handle its rehearsal space?
context: A four-piece band rehearses twice weekly and pays 18 per hour at a shared studio, about 300 a month. A private room costs 420 a month with a year lease; a garage offered by a member's parent is free but limits volume. They have a gig every three weeks.

options.name: keepshared
options.text: Stay with hourly shared studio bookings and keep full flexibility.

options.name: privateroom
options.text: Sign the year lease for a private room and split the cost four ways.

options.name: garage
options.text: Use the garage and install cheap acoustic panels for the neighbours.

options.name: shareprivate
options.text: Take the private room and sublet half the hours to another band.

options.name: electronic
options.text: Switch to electronic drums and amps so they can practise quietly at home.

decision: Which accounting setup should the six-person design studio choose?
context: A design studio has six staff, 480,000 revenue and a part-time bookkeeper who finds the current spreadsheets error-prone. Accounting software costs 40 a month, an outside accountant 450 a month, and tax deadlines recur quarterly. The owner has little time.

options.name: softwareonly
options.text: Adopt accounting software and let the bookkeeper run the books in it.

options.name: fullaccountant
options.text: Hand the books fully to an outside accountant on a monthly retainer.

options.name: softwareplus
options.text: Use accounting software and pay an outside accountant only at tax time.

options.name: improvesheets
options.text: Rebuild the spreadsheets with built-in checks and a monthly review.

options.name: morehours
options.text: Increase the bookkeeper's hours and keep the current spreadsheet methods.

options.name: bundledservice
options.text: Sign with a service that bundles software, bookkeeping and tax filing.

decision: How should the project tool change its pricing?
context: A project-management tool has 3,100 paying teams on a flat 12 per seat plan and a 3.5 percent monthly churn. Big accounts ask for custom features, while small teams complain about price. The team has two engineers focused on infrastructure for the next quarter.

options.name: threetiers
options.text: Introduce three tiers with feature limits and a cheaper small-team plan.

options.name: usagebased
options.text: Switch to usage-based pricing tied to the number of active projects.

options.name: annualdiscount
options.text: Keep the flat rate and add a 20 percent discount for annual payment.

options.name: freetier
options.text: Add a permanent free tier for tiny teams to feed the paid upgrade funnel.

options.name: enterprise
options.text: Keep the flat plan and add custom enterprise contracts for big accounts.

decision: How should the dairy farm store its winter feed?
context: A dairy farm of 70 cows needs about 220 tonnes of forage for winter and has a covered barn for 120 tonnes. Round bales wrapped in plastic cost 14 per tonne to wrap, a silage clamp costs 25,000 to build, and buying feed later costs 30 percent more. Wet summers are becoming common.

options.name: wrappedbales
options.text: Make wrapped round bales and store them outdoors on a hardcore pad.

options.name: silageclamp
options.text: Build a concrete silage clamp and fill it with the first grass cut.

options.name: drybarn
options.text: Make dry hay for the barn and buy the remaining shortfall in winter.

options.name: silagebags
options.text: Use large silage bags, bought in whatever quantity the farm needs.

options.name: fwdcontract
options.text: Contract with a neighbour to supply part of the feed at a fixed price.

options.name: lessherd
options.text: Reduce the herd by ten cows so that feed needs match the barn space.

decision: How should the vineyard staff its two-week grape harvest?
context: A family vineyard of 12 hectares must pick grapes in a 14-day window set by sugar levels. Seasonal crews cost 17 per hour and are hard to book, a harvesting machine can be rented for 3,000 a day and may bruise some fruit. Family members can work evenings only.

options.name: handcrew
options.text: Book a hand-picking crew early and bring in the whole crop over ten days.

options.name: machinerent
options.text: Rent the machine for four days and finish the whole harvest quickly.

options.name: mixedharvest
options.text: Machine-pick the cheaper grape blocks and hand-pick the premium blocks.

options.name: neighbourswap
options.text: Swap labour with two neighbouring vineyards on staggered picking dates.

options.name: volunteerday
options.text: Run a paid-in-wine volunteer weekend to cover part of the picking work.

decision: What format should the local arts magazine move to?
context: A quarterly arts magazine prints 1,200 copies at 3.10 each, sells 700 by subscription and shop, and loses about 3,500 a year. The editor wants more reach, advertisers prefer print, and two volunteers handle layout. Postage rose 15 percent this year.

options.name: stayprint
options.text: Keep the quarterly print run and cut page counts to reduce the cost.

options.name: digitalonly
options.text: Move to a digital-only edition with a paywalled back-issue archive.

options.name: twiceyear
options.text: Publish two larger print issues a year plus a monthly email newsletter.

options.name: newsletterweb
options.text: Replace print with a free web edition that advertisers help to fund.

options.name: printondemand
options.text: Print on demand in small batches and sell mainly at local arts events.

decision: How should the small publisher license its new textbook?
context: A small publisher has a 300-page introductory statistics textbook. Print sales to universities are 2,500 copies at 55, but students increasingly pirate PDFs. Open licensing could win adoption, while a bundled online platform costs 18,000 to build.

options.name: traditional
options.text: Sell it conventionally in print and as a locked digital edition.

options.name: openfree
options.text: Release it free under an open licence and sell print copies.

options.name: subscription
options.text: Sell institutional subscriptions with online exercises included.

options.name: rentaledition
options.text: Offer a low-cost 180-day digital rental alongside print.

options.name: platformbundle
options.text: Build the online platform and sell a bundle with the book.

options.name: chapterpacks
options.text: Sell individual chapters and custom course packs to lecturers.

decision: What should the team do after repeated minor outages?
context: A service had five outages of 10-30 minutes in 3 months, each with a different trigger. Engineers are stretched across feature work, and leadership wants a visible response. A formal reliability project would take 6 weeks of two people.

options.name: rootcause
options.text: Run a six-week reliability project on the shared underlying causes.

options.name: blameless
options.text: Write short blameless reviews per outage and fix only direct causes.

options.name: chaostest
options.text: Introduce regular failure-injection drills for the whole platform team.

options.name: errorbudget
options.text: Adopt error budgets that pause feature work when reliability dips.

options.name: addmonitor
options.text: Invest in better monitoring to detect and diagnose problems faster.

decision: How should the online shop change its returns policy?
context: An online clothing shop has 22 percent returns, free return shipping costing 5.80 each, and 8,000 orders a month. Customers cite free returns as a reason to buy. Margins are 38 percent, and some returned items cannot be resold.

options.name: keepfree
options.text: Keep free returns and improve the size guides to reduce return rates.

options.name: paidreturns
options.text: Charge a flat return fee and refund it when customers exchange items.

options.name: creditonly
options.text: Offer free returns only as store credit and charge for cash refunds.

options.name: shortwindow
options.text: Cut the return window from 60 days to 21 days and enforce it firmly.

options.name: serialflag
options.text: Limit free returns for customers whose personal return rate is very high.

options.name: dropoffpoints
options.text: Offer free drop-off at partner points and charge for mailed returns.

decision: How should the warehouse cover the peak season shifts?
context: A warehouse with 40 permanent staff expects volumes to rise 60 percent for six weeks. Temp workers cost 16 per hour, take two days to train and have 25 percent no-shows. Overtime for permanent staff costs 1.5 times pay and fatigue raises error rates.

options.name: tempagency
options.text: Bring in 20 agency temps and train them all during the first week.

options.name: overtimeheavy
options.text: Cover the whole peak with permanent staff overtime on a shared rota.

options.name: secondshift
options.text: Add an evening shift with a mix of temps and permanent staff.

options.name: seasonalhires
options.text: Hire seasonal workers directly for better retention and easier training.

options.name: autopick
options.text: Rent conveyor equipment to cut the manual handling time per order.

options.name: limitpromo
options.text: Ask sales to spread promotions so that peak volumes rise by less.
